issues.body:
Found by the checkpoint-triage lane on b282a2c6.

**Symptom.** The pkg291 GPU patch tests fail when other GPU tests run before them in the same process, and pass on their own:
- Full GPU pass (`run_split.py --gpu-only`): `test_gpu_patched_move_100k_faster_than_reflatten` fails at line 214, `last_render_info()["gpu_scene_patched"] is False`.
- `pytest test_pkg287 test_pkg288 test_pkg289 test_pkg291 -m "not cpu"`: `test_gpu_patches_cached_scene_and_matches_fresh_render[software]` fails instead.
- Alone, and in the file-only run: 3/3 pass each. `pkg287+pkg291` and `pkg288+pkg291` pass.

**Hypothesis (by reading code, not yet confirmed).** `wfPatchRefit` (`src/gpu/wavefront/gpu_wavefront_snapshot.cu`) keeps the `Hittable* -> tri index` map in the process-global `WfContext`. It rebuilds the map only when `C.triIndexBvh != bvh || C.triIndexBuildCount != renderer.getBvhBuildCount()`. `bvhBuildCount_` is per-renderer, so every fresh renderer reads 1 after its first build. If a new renderer's `BVHAccel` lands at a freed renderer's address, the stale map is reused (ABA). Then `triIndexOf.find(h)` misses and the patch is refused, which is the observed symptom. If the triangle addresses are also reused, it could instead scatter geometry into wrong slots silently. That is reachable in Blender, where the viewport and F12 renderers come and go.

**Proposed fix (native, needs a build).** Reset the map key on every full upload, e.g. `C.triIndexBvh = nullptr;` in the `if (!reuse)` block next to `C.refitPatchable = ...`, or key the map on `cachedOwner` as well. A full re-flatten can reorder triangles anyway, so a map built before it is never valid after it.

**Verify:** rerun the full GPU pass, or the 4-file command above, and the pkg291 tests pass.
issues.title: pkg291 GPU in-place patch refused in long GPU runs: triIndexOf map keyed on raw BVHAccel* (suspected ABA)

issues.body:
The `phash <= 16` gate on reference-bank scene `sms-refractive-glass-sphere` (checked by `tests/test_pkg127_reference_gates_poly.py`) sits at the Monte Carlo noise floor. It passes only because `reference.png` is the same seed-17 noise realization the test renders, so any change to the sample stream fails it about half the time. This happened with pkg305 (#1003) and again with #1040.

Measured on CPU, 2026-10-03 (#1040 diagnosis):
- Two independent 4096-spp adaptive-off renders differ from each other by phash 14.
- Independent 1024-spp renders from the same engine differ pairwise by phash 12-22 (old and new adaptive engines alike).
- Old engine vs its own blessed reference at seeds 11/22/33: phash 18/24/16.
- Fixed engine vs an independent 4096-spp adaptive-off reference: phash 20/14/18/12 at seeds 17/11/22/33. SSIM, delta-E and bright_coverage pass with wide margins.

pHash bits are the 8x8 low-frequency DCT terms compared with their median. On this mostly dark, smooth image many terms sit near the median and flip with noise (camera->glass->light fireflies).

Fix direction (pick one, measure flip rates first): a seed-robust metric (e.g. pHash on a downsampled/blurred image, or exclude bits within a noise margin of the median), or a multi-seed reference with the gate judged over N seeds. Do not just raise the threshold.

#1040 re-blessed the reference at seed 17 on the fixed engine as a stopgap (same precedent as pkg305).
issues.title: reference-bank phash gate (sms-refractive-glass-sphere) sits at the MC noise floor; needs seed-robust metric or multi-seed reference

issues.body:
Follow-ups from the Terra review of lane at-n1 (#991 Light Path, #990 Attributes). None blocked the PR.

1. GPU uploader second triangle pass: `src/gpu/scene_upload.cu` builds per-triangle attribute-layer corner slices during the geometry walk. A layer first read by a Light Path switch child (materialized afterwards, e.g. `Mix Shader(Is Camera Ray, plain A, Color Attribute-driven B)`) has no slices, so Attribute / Color Attribute / Object Info read 0 on GPU when B is selected (CPU is correct). The uploader prints `[#990] DEGRADED`. Fix: after the lpPending loop, a second pass over triangles filling slices for layers added late.
2. Missing Attribute Alpha default: the addon writes 1.0 for a missing Attribute alpha layer on bulk geometry, but the engine lookup (CPU `AttributeTexture` in `include/advanced_features.h`, GPU `gpu_attrTexel` in `shading_inputs_eval.cu`) returns 0 for any absent layer on non-bulk geometry. Verify the correct value against Cycles' attribute not-found behaviour in `intern/cycles/kernel/svm/attribute.h` (svm_node_attr, ATTR_STD_NOT_FOUND -> alpha 1), then make the engine default match.
3. Known (already tracked): shadow-ray Mix Shader selection uses only LPF_SHADOW, so Is Singular Ray / Is Reflection Ray choose Fac=0 on shadow rays; Cycles reads them from the parent path_flag.
4. LOW: GPU packed path counters saturate at 63 (diffuse/glossy/transmission) and 31 (transparent depth); CPU keeps 16-bit counters, so Light Path depth outputs diverge on very long paths.
issues.title: Light Path / Attribute follow-ups: GPU late switch-child attribute slices, missing Attribute Alpha default, counter saturation

issues.body:
Found by the Terra review of the #959 branch (lane/au-caustic). The pattern predates that branch: it has been here since pkg111.

The photon-map gather evaluates the caustic at any non-emissive first hit as `albedo/Ï€ Ã— density`. A glossy, metallic or coated receiver therefore gets a diffuse estimate, which is biased: it is too bright on rough metal and lacks view dependence.

Fix direction: evaluate the receiver BSDF for the photon's incoming direction (as Mitsuba's photon mapper does), or restrict the gather to the diffuse lobe and leave the glossy lobes to path tracing / MNEE. Needs a corpus scene with a caustic landing on a rough metal floor, plus a Mitsuba reference.

Related: #959, #1044.
issues.title: Photon caustic gather assumes a Lambertian receiver (albedo/pi) on glossy/metal surfaces

issues.body:
Found in the #959 lane (au-caustic). Since #959 the CPU path tracer builds the photon map whenever `usePhotonCaustics` is set (the addon sets it when a caster is flagged), matching the GPU estimator. ROI means agree with the GPU and an independent oracle (arb_prism_sun beams 0.998-1.002), but the CPU traces ONE 3M-photon map per render() call while the GPU (#909) traces a fresh 4M map every 16 spp (<= 256 maps). In sparse regions (photons scattered off the v2_dispersion_caustics ball lens / prism) the CPU gather shows coloured disc speckle of radius r_max that does not fall with spp (frozen); at 256 spp the GPU has ~64x more photons and averages it away.

Fix direction (stochastic PPM rounds, Hachisuka & Jensen 2009 / Knaus & Zwicker 2011, as on the GPU): render the CPU sample loop in rounds of N spp with a freshly seeded map per round (needs the per-pixel accumulators in raytracer.h's tile loop to persist across rounds; an Integrator::beginRound hook). Lead decision 2026-10-03: separate from the #959 PR.

Evidence: v2_dispersion_caustics CPU 256 spp vs GPU 1024 spp sheets in the #959 PR.
issues.title: CPU photon caustics: one 3M-photon map per render freezes gather speckle (GPU traces a fresh map every 16 spp)

issues.body: Found by Terra review of lane au-coords (#1006). Object (#1006) and Generated (#847) coordinates are per-vertex attributes baked at the shutter-open pose; CPU `Triangle::interpolateAt` (include/astroray/shapes.h) and GPU `gpu_objectCoord` / `gpu_generatedCoord` (src/gpu/wavefront/stage_advance_device.cuh) recompute barycentrics from the hit point against the STATIC (shutter-open) vertices. For a motion-blurred object (add_triangles_bulk_motion) the hit at time t lies on the interpolated triangle, so the barycentrics and hence the pattern slide with the motion instead of staying attached (Cycles: object_inverse_position_transform with the motion-interpolated object transform, svm/tex_coord.h). Fix: barycentrics from the motion-interpolated vertices at the ray time (or carry the hit barycentrics), CPU + GPU. Currently reported as an APPROXIMATED degradation by the addon for Object coordinates. Test: a translating object with Object-coordinate noise renders the same pattern as the static object at shutter centre.
issues.title: Object / Generated texture coordinates slide under motion blur (shutter-open barycentrics)

issues.body: Split out of #884 (u842 comment, 2026-09-25) so #884 can close on its clamp metric. CPU (principled Transparent lobe) and GPU (stage_advance.cu transparent continuation) increment `bounce` on an alpha/transparent pass-through. Cycles path_state_next early-returns for transparent and counts it in transparent_bounce (kernel/integrator/path_state.h, Apache-2.0). Effects: NEE at a surface seen through alpha is clamped with sample_clamp_indirect, emission hits after a pass-through use the indirect limit, and alpha spends the max_bounces budget. Needs a separate transparent-bounce counter ignored by the clamp sites and the depth limit (raytracer.h notes transparent limits are unwired, pkg201 S3). Gate: alpha-plane-over-lit-floor scene, clamp_indirect 10 vs 0 identical (as Cycles), transparent_max_bounces honoured.
issues.title: Transparent pass-throughs count as bounces (clamp class, max_bounces budget) unlike Cycles transparent_bounce

issues.body:
Found in lane au-media (#961/#1019 fix, branch lane/au-media). After the light-tree segment pick fix, v2_media converges as 1/N (CPU N x relVar 34.9 / 33.1 / 30.5 at 16 / 64 / 256 spp; was 69 / 461 / 115), but the smoke_plume ROI still has N x relVar ~80-96 vs Cycles 1.2 (power sampler 31x, so not the light pick).

Cause (by reading, not yet ablated): the #925/#929 segment direct light draws its distance strategy from a lane mixture of truncated exponentials at the media hull's GLOBAL majorant (sum of per-medium maxDensity x extinction). For a sparse dense VDB (density 10) the samples pile up at the AABB entry or land in empty space, and the equiangular strategy about a far lamp is near-uniform over the hull, so the lit skin of the plume is rarely sampled. Cycles' distance strategy is the null-scattering tracked scatter collision with octree local majorants, MIS'd with equiangular via the null-scattering path pdf (Miller et al. 2019; kernel/integrator/shade_volume.h volume_direct_scatter_mis / volume_integrate_step_scattering, Apache-2.0). The pkg267 DDA majorant grid (include/astroray/volume/majorant_grid.h) exists but is not wired into tracking or the segment NEE.

Scope: CPU boundedSegmentDirect + GPU gpu_volumeSegmentDirect (kind 0); first an ablation (vb0, NEE-only, equiangular-only/distance-only) to confirm the owner, then a local-majorant (or tracked-collision) distance strategy with its exact pdf for MIS. Gate: smoke_plume per-sample relVar within 3x Cycles, means in band. Related: pkg306, #1019.
issues.title: Media: heterogeneous segment-NEE distance strategy uses the hull's global majorant (smoke VDB per-sample variance ~75x Cycles)

issues.body: Found by pkg314 (lane at-n2). The <HasProgram=true> lambertian base-colour block in src/gpu/wavefront/stage_advance_device.cuh runs the op-VM only when matTexId >= 0, so a Diffuse BSDF whose Color is a chain over per-hit inputs only (Layer Weight / Fresnel / Backfacing -> ... , no texture, #989) renders the constant colour on GPU while the CPU evaluates it per hit. The Principled base-colour path (gpu_principledBaseTexel) handles texId -1. Repro: tests/test_pkg314_shader_graph_ir.py::test_shading_context_normal_ignores_bump[True-opvm] compared to the CPU leg. The pkg314 graph-program path does not have the gap (graph base colour is read from the graph kernel output). Fix: either route such programs through graph programs or let the lambertian block evaluate a program with texId -1.
issues.title: GPU skips a texture-less (per-hit only) op-VM program on a lambertian base colour (Diffuse + Layer Weight renders the constant)

issues.body:
Follow-up from #1020 (fix branch lane/as-arb).

After #1020 the film converts XYZ to linear sRGB with the exact IEC 61966-2-1 matrix, then clips negative channels to 0 per channel (beauty and each light-path pass separately). Out-of-gamut colours (narrow-band lamps, dispersion caustics) therefore lose their negative channel: a sodium lamp renders B = 0 where Mitsuba writes -0.096 (pkg307 narrow-band wall).

Consequences:
- Sum-to-beauty for light-path passes holds exactly only when no pass has a negative channel: clipping is nonlinear, so sum(max(pass, 0)) != max(sum(pass), 0) in the clipped channel. Before #1020 the desaturation made it worse (mismatch in all channels). Codex Terra review of the #1020 fix.
- Per-pixel clipping of noisy out-of-gamut estimates biases those channels upward at low spp.

Decision needed: should beauty/passes keep negative scene-linear values (Cycles and Mitsuba write them to EXR), and where should clipping happen instead (display transform, PNG/8-bit outputs, denoiser input)? Touches every film site listed in include/astroray/spectral.h xyzToLinearSRGBExact callers plus downstream consumers (addon result passes, OIDN, tests that assume >= 0).
issues.title: Film: out-of-gamut channels clipped to 0 per pass/beauty; decide whether scene-linear output keeps negative values

With the pkg305 stratified camera group the CPU noise floor at 4096 spp is gone, so the subtraction no longer hides the GPU bake error (CUDA builds, `astra_run/AP/ap-305/p277.py`):

| build | warped frac(gpu,cpu) | warped floor | plain frac(gpu,cpu) | plain floor | delta |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| main f0f8b5f6 | 0.730 | 0.230 | 0.204 | 0.135 | 0.430 |
| pkg305 | 0.690 | 0.0002 | 0.082 | 0.0000 | 0.608 |

The raw GPU-vs-CPU difference is unchanged (mean abs 0.1615 vs 0.1623; cell flips > 0.3: 0.223 vs 0.228). issues.body:
Follow-ups left open by pkg299 Phase 0/1 (OptiX hardware traversal, default on for triangle-only scenes):

1. **Time to first sample.** The GPU path still runs the CPU BVH build and the host flatten/upload (`buildAcceleration()` + `buildSceneArrays`) before the OptiX accel build. The spec's criterion is that the heavy scene's first call drops by at least 1.5 s. The software BVH also still backs the photon pre-pass, ReSTIR, SMS and the transparent-shadow walk, so each of those needs an OptiX route or an explicit fallback first.
2. **Refit on transform-only edits.** A pkg114 transform edit invalidates the scene cache, so every GAS and the IAS are rebuilt (62 ms per render on the 2M-triangle Cornell). This should refit or rebuild only the IAS and keep the GAS.
3. **Shared OptiX context with the denoiser.** Traversal (`src/gpu/optix/optix_pipeline.cpp`) and the pkg70 denoiser each create their own `OptixDeviceContext` on the same CUDA primary context, with separate function tables via `OPTIX_ENABLE_SDK_MIXING`.
4. **Transparent-shadow walk.** Scenes with Principled alpha < 1 (`HasAlphaShadow`) still trace shadow rays on the software BVH, while closest hits use OptiX. The walk could move into `__raygen__shadow` (closest-hit loop plus a material alpha lookup).

Phase 2 (spheres, curves, motion) is tracked in the pkg299 spec itself.

issues.body:
The pkg284 corpus v2 bands (`gates_v2.toml`, `mc_tolerance.py`) take the Astroray CPU sigma from seeds 278-282. The CPU tile loop seeds its white-noise stream as `mt19937(seed + tileIndex)`, so seed s+1 replays seed s shifted by one tile. The five renders are correlated and the per-ROI CPU sigma is underestimated.

Measured (CPU, 64 spp, main 775a5d6b, `astra_run/AP/ap-305/renders`), relative sigma of the ROI mean:

| ROI | seeds 278-282 (= toml `cpu_sigma`) | 15 independent seeds (278 + 10000 k) |
|---|---|---|
| v2_camera_geometry mesh_volume g | 0.0068 | 0.0105 |
| v2_camera_geometry mesh_volume L | 0.0072 | 0.0107 |
| v2_dispersion_caustics beam_through_prism L | 0.0156 | 0.0257 |

Effect: single-seed (278) rows whose Astroray mean sits a little off Cycles fail whenever the random stream changes. pkg305 (stratified camera group) changes it: `mesh_volume` g/b/L (0.974 vs tol 0.022) and `beam_through_prism` L (0.941 vs pin tol 0.0585) fail at seed 278, although their 15-seed means equal the baseline (mesh_volume L 0.9855 vs 0.9849; beam new/base 0.996).

Fix: re-derive the bands with independent seeds (e.g. `--seeds 278 10278 20278 30278 40278`) for the Cycles, CPU and GPU legs, then remove the provisional rows that cite this issue.
issues.title: Corpus v2 bands: CPU sigma from correlated seeds 278-282 is underestimated (mt19937 seed+tile streams overlap)

## Context

pkg265 (PR #778) implements the Heitz 2016 multiple-scattering microfacet dielectric random walk for rough glass, replacing the single-scatter + pkg264 #771 dead-sample delta reroute. The walk uses a **plain-dielectric** Fresnel/transmission coefficient in its phase function.

The second cycles-parity review (CRITICAL #2) found that a **thin-film** rough Principled glass (thin_film_thickness > cutoff, roughness > kDeltaGlassRoughness) was being routed through this plain-dielectric walk. The walk:
- sets `isDelta=true` (skip-NEE contract) but `eval()`/`pdf()` still return the nonzero thin-film single-scatter f for a thin-film glass â†’ **direct light double-counted** (NEE + full-weight emitter hit) up to ~2x on the directly-lit part;
- carries plain-dielectric Fresnel throughput â†’ **drops the iridescence colour** on the sampled path.

## Fix landed in #778

Thin-film rough glass is gated OUT of the walk (`filmActive()` branch in `principled.cpp` `chooseAndSampleDir` + `transmissionPdf`): it falls back to the origin/main single-scatter rough-transmission sampler (incl. the pkg264 #771 reroute), so sample == eval == pdf are all single-scatter thin-film, no double count, iridescence preserved on the eval path. Disney glass has no thin-film path, so no change there.

## This follow-up

Make the multiple-scattering walk **thin-film-aware**: replace the plain-dielectric Fresnel/transmission coefficient in the Heitz dielectric phase function (`include/astroray/microsurface_dielectric.h`) with the thin-film iridescence Fresnel/transmittance (the `thin_film_fresnel.h` coefficients already used by `transmissionEvalRGB`/`transmissionEvalSpectral`), so thin-film rough glass gets the physically-correct multiple-scattering treatment AND its iridescence colour on every bounce of the walk. Then the `filmActive()` single-scatter fallback in `principled.cpp` can be removed.

Non-trivial: the walk crosses the interface many times with alternating entering/exiting film-IOR adjustment; the per-bounce thin-film transmittance must telescope correctly (cf. the etaÂ² telescoping validated in `test_pkg265_walk_eta.cpp`).

Priority: P2 (the #778 fix is correct and unbiased; this is a quality/parity improvement for the thin-film-glass corner).

## Summary
Cycles supports holdout objects (cut a hole in the render for compositing) and indirect-only objects (visible in reflections/GI but not directly).

## Cycles reference
- `intern/cycles/kernel/integrator/shade_surface.h` â€” holdout handling
- `intern/cycles/scene/object.cpp` â€” `is_shadow_catcher`, `use_holdout`

## What to implement
1. **Holdout**: when a camera ray hits a holdout object, set alpha=0 and color=0 (creates a hole)
2. **Indirect only**: object is invisible to camera rays but visible to all other rays (reflections, GI, shadows)
3. Read `obj.is_holdout` and collection `holdout` property during export
4. Store the flag per-primitive and check in `pathTrace()`

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A holdout sphere creates a black hole with alpha=0 in the render
- [ ] An indirect-only object appears in mirror reflections but not in the direct camera view
